pr_title: Add unsigned variants for BitConverter float bit APIs
pr_body:
Adds DoubleToUInt64Bits, UInt64BitsToDouble, SingleToUInt32Bits,
UInt32BitsToSingle, HalfToUInt16Bits and UInt16BitsToHalf.

Implementations were based on existing signed integer variants.

Convert usages of existing APIs to unsigned variants when appropriate.

Fix #36469

The changes build on my machine, but I was unable to run the unit tests, running all of them made the test process hang for 4 hours, so I'm opening this to see what happens on the CI.

issue_context.title: Consider adding SingleToUInt32Bits(float value) to BitConverter
comments:
Is it really that hard to cast to `uint` as needed in this case? 

There are many APIs in .NET that return `int` and where `uint` is sometime more convenient for micro-optimizations. I do not think it makes sense to add `uint` variants to all these APIs.

Tagging subscribers to this area: @tannergooding
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.
I'm going to mark this as `ready-for-review` and we can have further discussion on whether or not this is warranted in API review. We already have these methods internally.

> We already have these methods internally.

Pointers? I do not think we have them in any shipping binaries.

> Pointers? I do not think we have them in any shipping binaries.

Ah, you're right, I was misremembering.

We just have many of the internally usages in product code explicitly converting to the unsigned variant:
* https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/BitConverter.cs,27a5a69559e7663e,references
* https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/BitConverter.cs,db20ea77a561c0ac,references
* https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/BitConverter.cs,bd24ba94db019618,references

I'd like to try and do this, if I understand correctly `src\libraries\System.Private.CoreLib\src\System\BitConverter.cs` is the place for API implementation, `src\libraries\System.Runtime\ref\System.Runtime.cs` for the reference and `src\libraries\System.Runtime.Extensions\tests\System\BitConverter.cs` for the unit tests, is there any other place that needs changing?

> is there any other place that needs changing?

The APIs would need to be expose, tests added, and ideally all the existing usages would be updated to use the new APIs as appropriate: https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/BitConverter.cs,27a5a69559e7663e,references.
This would include places that are directly doing `(uint)BitConverter.SingleToInt32Bits(value);` (such as https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/BinaryWriter.cs,309)
As well as places that are correctly using things like `unchecked((int)(0x80000000))` after getting the signed bits (such as https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/MathF.cs,73)
Okay, I've implemented the APIs itself and unit tests for them locally, should I open a draft before I go over all the existing usages  or do that and then open a PR?

> should I open a draft before I go over all the existing usages or do that and then open a PR

I don't have a preference myself. That being said, we prefer to not keep draft PRs open for too long so it would likely be good to wait if you don' think you'll be able to get the remaining changes up within a few days of creating the draft.

@MichalPetryka, are you still working on this?

If so, it would be great to get a PR up so we can get this into .NET 6. And if not, please let me know and I can pick it up and finish it out (even using your existing changes/commits if that's alright with you)
Sorry, I've had some trouble running the tests (wasn't able to start them at all, even without any changes) and then I got sick and forgot about this. I'll get back to this tommorow.
